sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Lord Buddha is depicted ______ and in human form in Ajanta paintings.
The Ajanta caves are located near ______ district in Maharashtra.
The depiction of ______ is particularly noteworthy in Ajanta.
The Black Princess is a testament to the artist's ______.
The colours used in Ajanta paintings are simple and ______, not loud.

sections.passage: The Ajanta caves are located near Aurangabad district in Maharashtra. Ajanta paintings hold a unique place in the history of Indian painting. Buddha is depicted in symbolic and human forms in Ajanta paintings. The Ajanta paintings were created in Buddhist stupas and chaityas, and the depiction of women is particularly noteworthy. Black Princess is considered one of the finest works among the Ajanta paintings: the free lines, the delicate harmony of the body parts, the slight tilt of the face and the curves of the eyes show the artist's mastery. The colours used are very simple and earthy and not loud. (April 2026)

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The Indus Valley Civilization is also known as the ______ Civilization.
The civilization flourished between 2500 BC and ______ BC.
The Mauryan dynasty was founded by ______.
______ the Great erected pillars all over the empire.
Ashoka was a follower of ______.

sections.passage: The Indus Valley Civilization was named after the site from where the first evidence of the civilization was found. Main sites are Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. It is also known as the Harappan Civilization and flourished between 2500 BC and 1750 BC. The next important period was the time of the Mauryan dynasty, founded by Chandragupta Maurya. His grandson Ashoka the Great contributed much to art and architecture; he followed Buddhism and erected pillars all over the empire to spread the teachings of Lord Buddha. (April 2024)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: The Gupta period is regarded as the golden period of Indian art history.
Sarnath and Mathura were art centres in the Gupta period.
The slight tilt of the lip is a stylistic feature of the Guptas.
Temple architecture started at Udaygiri in Gujarat.
questions.answer: False – the Udaygiri caves and Nachna and Bhumara are in Madhya Pradesh.

sections.passage: The Gupta period is regarded as the golden period of Indian art history. Refinement came in the representation of the human figures. Some of the most important art centres during this period were Mathura, Sarnath, Ujjain and Ahichhatra. The slight tilt of the lip, the full roundness of the figures, accurate carvings and simplicity became the stylistic stamp of the Guptas. Famous paintings of Ajanta were done during this period. The Udaygiri caves in Madhya Pradesh and the places Nachna and Bhumara show the beginning of temple architecture. (October 2025)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: The Dancing Girl is a metal statue.
She is shown wearing heavy clothes.
questions.answer: False – she is shown without clothes.

questions.q: Her hair is tied in a bun.
She was found at Ajanta.
questions.answer: False – she was found at Mohenjo-daro.

sections.passage: The Dancing Girl is made of metal and is probably one of the finest examples of the artistic and technical skills of Indus Valley craftsmen. The figure is lanky, thin and rhythmic. She is shown without clothes, with bangles on her left arm up to almost the shoulder. Her hair is tied in a bun. She stands in a resting posture with her right hand at her waist and left hand on her left thigh. It was found at Mohenjo-daro and is about 4 inches in height, yet it seems larger.

questions.q: Describe the Dancing Girl and mention its finding site.
questions.answer: The Dancing Girl is a metal statue of about 4 inches height from the Harappan period (2500 BC), found at Mohenjo-daro and now in the National Museum, New Delhi. The figure is lanky, thin and rhythmic, without clothes, with bangles on the left arm and hair tied in a bun; she stands in a resting posture with her right hand at the waist. It shows fine metal casting.

questions.q: Write the characteristics of the Rampurva Bull Capital.
questions.answer: It is made of polished sandstone (Mauryan, 3rd century BC) with a bell-shaped inverted lotus as base, an abacus with plant designs and a majestic bull on top. The plain bull contrasts with the ornate lotus and abacus and shows the weight and power of the animal. Its extremely high polish is a main characteristic of Mauryan sculpture.

questions.q: Describe the base and material of the Bull Capital.
questions.answer: The base is an inverted bell-shaped lotus with an abacus above it carrying plant designs; the capital is made of polished sandstone and is about 7 ft high.

questions.q: Write a short note on the 'Black Princess' of the Ajanta paintings.
questions.answer: The Black Princess is a mural in tempera from the Gupta–Vakataka period (2nd–6th century AD), about 20 ft x 6 ft, in the Mahayana phase at Ajanta. Its free-flowing line, subtle rhythm of the body contour, slight tilt of the face and curved eyes show the artist's mastery; the colours are earthy, with a lyrical and heavenly quality.

questions.q: What are the characteristics of Ajanta paintings?
questions.answer: They were done in two phases (Hinayana – Buddha in symbols; Mahayana – in human form) in tempera, not fresco. The themes are mainly religious but have scope for creativity; women are shown beautifully; the line is flowing, the colours are earthy and the paintings can be enjoyed by common people.

questions.q: Where are the Ajanta caves? In which phase of Ajanta painting was the Black Princess done?
questions.answer: The Ajanta caves are near Aurangabad in Maharashtra, named after the village Ajintha. The Black Princess was done in the Mahayana phase (Gupta–Vakataka period).

questions.q: What was the contribution of the Kushans to Indian art?
questions.answer: The Kushans came from outside India but helped the progress of Indian art; during their time sculpted portraiture developed for the first time.

questions.q: What are the specialities of Mauryan sculptures?
questions.answer: The Ashokan pillars have an extremely polished surface, a base, a shaft and a capital with animals on an abacus over an inverted lotus; the carving of animals shows mastery, and the technique of high polish was learnt from the Middle East.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: Give a description of the works of the Indus Valley Civilization.
questions.answer: The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization flourished between 2500 and 1750 BC with main sites at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. Great numbers of art objects and antiquities have been found: seals, pottery, jewellery, tools, toys, statuettes and utilitarian objects. The Dancing Girl in metal shows fine casting and a rhythmic figure; mother-goddess figures in crude folk style were also made.

questions.q: 'Black Princess' is no doubt one of the best examples of Ajanta painting. Why?
questions.answer: The free-flowing line, the subtle rhythm of the body contour, the slight tilt of the face and the curves of the eyes show the artist's control over the brush. Even the damaged painting shows how beautiful the colours were; they are earthy and soft, and there is a lyrical, heavenly quality in the softness of the contour and the bending of the neck.

questions.q: Why is the Gupta period called the golden or classical period of Indian art?
questions.answer: Refinement came in the human figure; sculptures show a perfect balance of style, skill and imagination, and religious sculptures have a divine quality; the stylistic stamp was the slight tilt of the lip, roundness of the figures, accurate carving and simplicity; secular sculpture was also produced; Ajanta paintings and cave and temple architecture developed; and arts and sciences all progressed.

questions.q: Write about Mauryan art.
questions.answer: The Mauryan period (3rd century BC) was a new beginning. Ashoka erected pillars with edicts and Buddha's teachings in almost every region of India; each pillar has a base, shaft and capital with animal figures on an abacus above an inverted lotus. The sculptures are extremely polished and show mastery in carving animals, as in the Rampurva Bull Capital in polished sandstone.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the Dancing Girl of the Indus Valley and its characteristics.
questions.answer: The Dancing Girl (metal, Harappan period, 2500 BC, Mohenjo-daro, about 4 inches, National Museum, New Delhi) is one of the finest examples of Indus Valley metal casting. The figure is lanky, thin and rhythmic. She is shown without clothes, with bangles from her wrist almost to the shoulder of her left arm, like tribal people of Gujarat and Rajasthan today. Her hair is tied in a bun, a contemporary style. She stands in a resting posture with the right hand at her waist and the left hand on her left thigh. The casting is perfect, and the little statue has great monumentality.

questions.q: Explain the Rampurva Bull Capital as a work of Mauryan art.
questions.answer: It is a polished sandstone Ashokan capital of about 7 ft from Rampurva, now in the Indian Museum, Kolkata. It has a bell-shaped inverted lotus as base, an abacus with plant motifs and a majestic bull on top. The bull dominates the ornate lotus and abacus; the weight and power of the animal are felt and the unfinished stone between the legs does not disturb its beauty. The extremely high polish, learnt from Middle Eastern sculptors, is a main characteristic of Mauryan sculpture.

questions.q: Write an appreciation of the Ajanta painting 'Black Princess'.
questions.answer: The Black Princess is a Gupta–Vakataka mural (about 20 ft x 6 ft) in tempera from the Mahayana phase at Ajanta. The free-flowing line, subtle rhythm of the body contour, slight tilt of the face and curves of the eyes show the artist's mastery. Even the damaged painting shows the beauty of the colours, which are earthy and quiet. The softness of the contour and the subtle bending of the neck give it a heavenly, lyrical quality.
